long_biography.plain_text:
Niel co-founded Worldnet, France's first internet provider, in 1993 and later sold it for USD 50 million. He then launched Free, whose simple pricing and Freebox combined broadband, telephony and television. Those innovations helped Iliad challenge established operators and made telecom the foundation of his fortune.

Niel remains Iliad's chairman, but his present activity extends beyond the original group. Through NJJ Holding he oversees international telecom, media and real-estate investments, while Kima Ventures backs startups. He also established coding school 42 and Station F as practical infrastructure for technical education and entrepreneurship. These roles combine continuing founder control with broad capital allocation and institution-building.
